data.description: Standard base64 of the stored bytes, ready for an MCP image or text content block.

digest.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the stored bytes.

instanceId.description: Session this attachment is staged for; also the read-authorization key.

name.description: Derived `<objectId>.<ext>`; a caller-supplied filename never survives.

AttachmentUpload.description: Staged attachment metadata (D-027). The media type and name are the Hub's own: the type is sniffed from the bytes and the name is derived as <objectId>.<ext>, so a caller-supplied filename never survives.

digest.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the stored bytes.

expiresAt.description: RFC3339. Staging is lazily expired, not swept by a job.

children.description: Direct children created by this instance; descendants do not inherit scope.

origin.description: Authenticated origin; clients must treat an unknown origin as Agent.

EffortSelection.description: Native effort selection (D-028 §9.1): the harness-native level plus an orthogonal ultracode boolean (Claude only). Claude takes low | medium | high | xhigh | max; Codex and Grok add minimal on the low end. Legacy tier names (default / think / think-hard / ultra / ultracode) are accepted and normalized by NAME — never by index, because the old per-harness tables differed in length.

name.description: minimal | low | medium | high | xhigh | max (minimal is Codex/Grok-only), or a legacy tier name to be normalized.

ultracode.description: Dynamic workflow. Equivalent to xhigh plus dynamic workflow; session-only, never persisted as a level.

code.description: Machine-readable error code. Instance creation uses PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED for an explicit gateway request without a matching provider profile and PLACEMENT_UNSATISFIABLE for unsatisfied placement constraints.

FleetBroadcast.description: Select running instances and fan one command out. Requires `all` or at least one of `hosts` / `labels` / `kinds`; filters intersect. Agent broadcasts are checked before dispatch; cross-instance sends and all key input require Human approval.

all.description: Forbidden from Agent origin, even with filters. Human/Bot callers must also set confirm=true.

confirm.description: Explicit confirmation of an all broadcast; does not exempt Agent callers.

idempotencyKey.description: Base key; each instance is queued under `<key>:<instanceId>` so a retry replays instead of double-sending.

claudeBinaryPath.description: Per-host default claude executable. Empty string clears the default.

defaultLaunchArgs.description: Per-host default extra CLI args. Null clears the default.

claudeBinaryPath.description: Per-host default claude executable. Validated by the Node, not the Hub.

defaultLaunchArgs.description: Per-host default extra CLI args, used when a create omits args.

workspaceId.description: Canonical target workspace for a mutation

path.description: Absolute path on the Node, within its configured workspace roots

args.description: Extra native CLI arguments as an argv array, never a shell string. Checked against the per-driver launch allowlist; replaces the host default when present.

binaryPath.description: Host-absolute executable override. The Node validates and pins it; the Hub only stores the string.

binarySha256.description: Expected sha256: digest of binaryPath. The launch is refused when the Node's pin disagrees.

role.description: Preset name applied at create and stored for display; enforcement reads scope+grants, never this field (design §2.5).

worktree.description: Worktree name created by remuda worktree create.

nodePurge.description: Outcome of the Node `instance.purge` call; the Hub record is deleted either way.

token.description: Bearer credential; keep secret and do not journal it.

activity.description: idle only after a Node/herdr agent_status or session idle observation. Create default is unknown.

effortIndex.description: Legacy per-harness table index. Preserved for older clients; never used to derive the tier, because the old tables differed in length per harness.

effortName.description: Normalized D-028 §9.1 effort level. Legacy tiers stored on older rows are mapped by name on read (default→low, think→high, think-hard/ultra→xhigh, ultracode→xhigh with effortUltracode true). `minimal` is Codex/Grok-only and never emitted for a Claude launch.

effortUltracode.description: Dynamic-workflow flag (`--effort ultracode`). Session-only; it is xhigh plus dynamic workflow, not a sixth level.

launchedBy.description: Who ran the launch command (D-028 §1.0 rule 4). Provenance only, never a capability level: a user-launched session is entitled to exactly the same signals as a Remuda-launched one. Derived from mode/promotedAt for rows written before D-028.

lifecycle.description: Derived from Node lifecycle observations in journal.append. Create default is requested, not running.

mode.description: How this instance reached its kind. "promoted" means a terminal instance had a known agent CLI take over its PTY foreground (D-025); the driver stays shell-pty.

nativeSessionId.description: Native session id the driver reported; what POST /v1/instances/{id}/resume passes to `claude --resume` (D-026).

nativeTranscriptPath.description: Native transcript path, when a driver reported one (D-026).

parentInstanceId.description: Immutable creator instance, recorded by the Hub from authenticated identity.

promotedAt.description: When the terminal was promoted. Absent unless mode is "promoted".

resumedFrom.description: Exited instance whose conversation this instance continues (D-026).

signalTier.description: Signal tier confirmed by the Node for the current native session. Absent until a tier has been observed.

InstanceScope.description: Delegation-tree resource reach (design §2.5). Empty dimensions mean 'not narrowed'; child scope must be a subset of the parent.

supplyGrants.description: Provider profile ids this node may spend (structured grants land with co-supply).

thisDevice.description: Whether this passkey was registered from the device making the request.

options.description: WebAuthn options object (PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions for register, PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions for login).

assertion.description: AuthenticatorAssertionResponse PublicKeyCredential as produced by navigator.credentials.get; rawId and response fields are base64url.

mediation.description: Set to conditional for WebAuthn conditional mediation (autofill); omit for the platform picker.

attestation.description: AuthenticatorAttestationResponse PublicKeyCredential as produced by navigator.credentials.create; rawId and response fields are base64url.

Project.description: Thin authoritative Hub Project entity; design §3.2.

coordinatorFanOut.description: Active children one node may delegate (Hub default 8).

ProjectEnforcedPolicy.description: D-031 enforced switches. All default true; read-only for coordinator agents after creation.

ProjectPatch.description: remuda project set. Enforced policy (D-031) is immutable after creation; only policy.configurable is applied.

ProjectProviderRef.description: Project never holds a secret, only a profileId and delegation shape.

defaultModel.description: Must be one of the enabled models.

ProviderDiscover.description: Probe a gateway before the profile exists. The token is used once and never echoed.

profileId.description: Reuse this saved profile's stored token, base URL and headers.

token.description: Auth token for an unsaved profile. Never returned.

surfaces.description: Gateway listings that reported this id (`anthropic`, `openai`). A gateway may serve a different catalog per header, so the probe unions both. Empty for a manually typed id.

ProviderModelInput.description: A model id, or a structured entry. Bare strings migrate to enabled entries.

labels.description: Placement labels such as egress:gateway or region=sg.

target.description: SSH config alias or user@host, resolved by the Hub system SSH client.

workspaceId.description: Registered workspace containing the repository; omitted selects the Node default.

get.description: Backs the in-session MCP tool `remuda_attachment`. Unlike `GET /v1/objects/{id}`, this route admits the instance credential the MCP server runs with, and pins the read to that credential's own session — not a child's, not a parent's. Bytes come back base64 in JSON because the caller is building an MCP content block. Attachments over 3670016 bytes (3.5 MiB, mirroring the claude-print inline budget) are refused with RESOURCE_LIMIT naming the size and media type. Expired objects read as 404.

delete.description: Removes the Hub record (journal, commands, interactions, fleet membership) and asks the owning Node to purge its per-instance data directory. The agent's own native transcripts under the user's home are never touched. Human and Bot devices only; agents receive 403. A live Instance is refused with 409 unless `force=1`, which stops it and settles it as `exited` first. A repeated delete returns 404, so the call is idempotent.
